fields.why: The overall 21.6% and 28.4% are the two values of the 2021 vs 2022 contrast, and the brief says the values of a contrast do not earn summary; no single-group result stands alone.
A QuickStats has no Summary; its first sentence leads with 2021 vs 2022 (pair), while falling back to group > pair gives group for the three age groups compared within each year.
The brief says two time points compared count as before/after, and the headline claim is the 2021 to 2022 increase; cross-sectional from the NHIS household interview is also right.

The text reports 0-5 vs 6-11 and 12-17 in 2021 and 12-17 vs 6-11 in 2022, then says 'Other observed differences among age groups were not significant', so every pair was tested with no single referent.

brief_issues: The framework-lead rule cites the Summary's headline claim; QuickStats and other reports without a Summary need a rule (e.g. treat the first sentence as the headline, or apply group > pair).
